# Peggy Guggenheim in London

The Making of a Collector

##### 21 November 2026 - 14 March 2027

The Jillian and Arthur M. Sackler Wing of Galleries | Burlington House

**Tues–Thurs & Sun:** 10am–6pm  
**Fri–Sat:** 10am–9pm

**Tickets £17**

[Book now](https://my.royalacademy.org.uk/events/ex-peggy-guggenheim)

Friends of the RA go free

In the late 1930s, Peggy Guggenheim launched an art gallery in Mayfair that shocked the conservative tastes of the British art establishment. This exhibition revisits the gallery that helped redefine London’s contemporary art scene.

It’s January 1938. The American collector and patron Peggy Guggenheim has just opened her first gallery on Cork Street, just around the corner from the Royal Academy. Over the next year and a half, 'Guggenheim Jeune' will become one of the radical voices for progress amid London's conservative art institutions, promoting works affiliated with Surrealism and abstraction that will change the fate of contemporary art in Britain. She hosted over 20 exhibitions, including the first UK solo show of Vasily Kandinsky, the first exhibition of collage in Britain, and a contemporary sculpture exhibition that became a national scandal. **Our [Friends](https://www.royalacademy.org.uk/friends-of-the-royal-academy) preview days take place 18 November, 10am–6pm, 19 November, 10am–6pm, and 20 November, 10am–9pm.**
